about.title: About GIS–SAGAR
about.subtitle: Local evidence for groundwater recharge.
about.intro: GIS–SAGAR — Smart Application for Groundwater Artificial Recharge — helps people explore where recharge may be appropriate and which structures deserve site assessment.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.text: Groundwater supports homes, farms and communities. Where extraction exceeds replenishment, recharge planning needs to respond to local ground conditions. A structure that works at one location may not suit another.

sections.title: The gap we address
sections.text: The project began with two connected needs: wider access to practical geospatial tools and stronger participation by groundwater users. GIS–SAGAR brings mapped evidence into a workflow that communities and technical practitioners can discuss together.

sections.title: How it works
sections.text: Select a site, load observations and inspect a weighted screening score for each analysis cell. The application evaluates recharge structures against the available evidence and identifies the site checks needed before selection.

sections.title: Enabled for now
sections.text: Soil texture and slope are enabled for the current assessment. The configurable framework also retains geology, geomorphology, land cover, drainage, weathering thickness, groundwater depth and rainfall for staged integration as data and assessment rules become available.

sections.title: From evidence to action
sections.text: Recommendations are preliminary. Site observations and technical assessment are needed to confirm receiving-ground permeability, groundwater conditions, water quality and structural suitability. The application supports this assessment; it does not determine construction dimensions or recharge volumes.

sections.title: A community and climate purpose
sections.text: By making the evidence and outstanding checks visible, GIS–SAGAR aims to support informed local participation in water conservation and climate adaptation. Its value will be assessed through site verification and future field use.

about.credit: Original project proposal: Anagha Raghunandan. This application develops the proposal’s focus on technology access and community participation.

help.title: Using GIS–SAGAR
help.subtitle: Select a site. Read the evidence. Check the conditions.
help.intro: Start with the saved test site, or import observations for your own boundary.

sections.title: 1 · Open a site
sections.text: Choose Load test site for the saved 100 m × 100 m example. For another location, open Site and enter coordinates, adjust the dimensions, import a boundary or draw one on the map. Changing the boundary clears its observations and recorded site conditions.

sections.title: 2 · Load observations
sections.text: Open Data, choose the soil source and import matching observations. OpenLandMap supplies texture classes at stated depths; SoilGrids supplies sand, silt and clay fractions for depth intervals. Source choice is explicit. Missing values are not filled from another dataset.

sections.title: 3 · Inspect the map
sections.text: Select a coloured cell to view its mapped soil, slope and screening score. The score expresses relative preference under the current settings, not recharge probability. A 30 m analysis grid does not increase the approximately 250 m soil-data resolution.

sections.title: 4 · Read recommendations
sections.text: Preliminary recommendations identify options for site assessment. Suitability unconfirmed means that an option still needs supporting field evidence. Limited screening support identifies a soil or slope constraint. Open Site checks for each option’s outstanding conditions. Structures excluded by recorded conditions are not suggested.

sections.title: 5 · Add site context
sections.text: Under Site → Site conditions, record whether a channel, tank or dug well is present, absent or unknown. Exclude a structure only after site review. Detailed infiltration, groundwater and water-quality measurements are not yet collected through dedicated forms.

sections.title: 6 · Adjust the model
sections.text: Open Settings to adjust the enabled factors’ location and structure weights. Existing observations are rescored without another data request. Additional factors need their own observations and assessment rules. Reset weights & rules returns to the baseline.

sections.title: 7 · Save the assessment
sections.text: Export results downloads a JSON snapshot containing observations, settings, recorded conditions and calculated results. Export settings saves the model configuration separately. Assessment state is held in the current page session.

sections.title: Live data
sections.text: The saved test data came from a real Earth Engine run. The hosted connection still requires backend configuration and validation. OpenLandMap currently uses the comparison-script/import workflow; the supplied hosted adapter must be extended before retrieving it directly.

help.credit: Use field verification and appropriate technical review before selecting or constructing a recharge intervention.
